topic_ko: A 씨와 B 씨 — 아깝게 놓칠수록 ‘만약 ~했더라면’을 더 되뇌며 더 속상해한다

passage: Mr. A and Mr. B got stuck in traffic and reached the airport thirty minutes late.
Mr. A learns that his flight left on time.
Mr. B learns that his flight was delayed and left only five minutes ago.
Most people think that Mr. B will feel much worse.
He keeps thinking, “If only we had taken another street.”
A tiny change could have saved his flight.
When we miss a goal by a lot, we rarely imagine a different result.
But when we miss it by a little, it hurts more, and we keep replaying the “what ifs.”
choices: how to avoid traffic jams on the way to the airport
why missing something by a little feels worse
the reasons flights are often delayed
how surveys are used to study people
why limousines are popular at airports
theme.explanation_ko: 5분 차이로 놓친 B 씨가 더 속상하듯, 아깝게 놓칠수록 더 아프다는 내용이므로 ②가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ① 교통 체증 피하는 법이 아니다. ③ 비행기 지연의 이유가 아니다. ④ 설문은 근거로만 쓰였다. ⑤ 리무진 이야기가 아니다.

passage: Two men missed their flights after a traffic jam.
One flight had left on time, but the other had left just five minutes earlier.
In a survey, 96 percent of people said the second man would be more upset.
This is because he can easily imagine how things could have been different.
A different street or a shorter stop might have changed everything.
When we fail by a wide margin, such thoughts do not come easily.
But a near miss stings, because success was so close.
The closer we are to success, the more we think about what might have been.
choices: 비행기를 놓치지 않으려면 일찍 출발해야 한다.
설문 조사의 결과는 항상 믿을 만하다.
성공에 가까이 갔다가 실패할수록 더 큰 아쉬움을 느낀다.
큰 차이로 실패할수록 더 오래 후회하게 된다.
교통 체증은 사람들을 가장 화나게 하는 일이다.
gist.explanation_ko: 아깝게 놓치면 다른 결과를 쉽게 상상할 수 있어 더 아프고, 성공에 가까울수록 더 많이 되뇐다는 내용이므로 ③이 요지이다.
gist.distractor_ko: ① 일찍 출발하라는 조언은 없다. ② 설문 결과의 신뢰성은 다루지 않는다. ④ 반대로 큰 차이로 실패하면 그런 생각이 잘 들지 않는다. ⑤ 교통 체증은 상황 설정일 뿐이다.

passage: Mr. A and Mr. B got stuck in traffic and reached the airport thirty minutes late.
Mr. A learns that his flight left on time.
Mr. B learns that his flight was delayed and left only five minutes ago.
Most people think that Mr. B will feel much worse.
He keeps thinking, “If only we had taken another street.”
A tiny change could have saved his flight.
When we miss a goal by a lot, we rarely imagine a different result.
But when we miss it by a little, it hurts more, and we keep replaying the “what ifs.”
choices: A Long Trip in a Limousine
title.explanation_ko: 성공에 가까웠던 만큼 더 아프다는 내용이므로 ④ ‘너무 가까웠기에 더 아픈’이 제목으로 알맞다.
title.distractor_ko: ① 비행기를 타는 요령이 아니다. ② 어느 길로 가야 하는지가 아니다. ③ 비행기 지연 이유가 아니다. ⑤ 리무진 여행기가 아니다.

passage: Mr. B arrived at the airport thirty minutes late.
His flight had been delayed, so it left just five minutes before he arrived.
He thinks, “If only we had taken Main Street.”
He also thinks, “If only the driver hadn’t stopped so long.”
His mind keeps replaying the “what ifs.”
Such thoughts are strongest when success was very close.
choices: watching a movie again and again
asking the airline for a new ticket
blaming other people for the traffic
imagining how small changes could have helped
implication.explanation_ko: “다른 길로 갔더라면”, “운전기사가 덜 멈췄더라면” 하고 되뇌는 것이므로 ⑤ ‘작은 변화가 어떻게 도움이 되었을지 상상하는 것’이다.
implication.distractor_ko: ① 다음 여행 계획이 아니다. ② 실제로 영화를 다시 보는 것이 아니다. ③ 새 표를 요청하는 내용은 없다. ④ 남을 탓하는 것이 아니라 가능했던 결과를 상상한다.

passage: Mr. A and Mr. B were scheduled leaving the airport at the same time.
They got caught in a traffic jam and arrived thirty minutes late.
When presented with this story, most people believed Mr. B would be more upset.
You can almost hear him say, “If only we had taken Main Street.”
The closer we are to success, the more our minds replay the “what ifs.”
grammar.explanation_ko: 「be scheduled + to부정사」 ‘~할 예정이다’이므로 were scheduled leaving 은 were scheduled to leave 가 되어야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ② get caught in ‘~에 갇히다’. ③ When (they were) presented — 접속사 뒤 주어+be 생략. ④ If only + 과거완료 ‘~했더라면’. ⑤ the 비교급, the 비교급 ‘~할수록 더 …하다’.

passage: Mr. A and Mr. B missed their flights because of a traffic jam.
Mr. B’s flight was delayed, so it left long before he arrived.
Most people think Mr. B would be more upset than Mr. A.
He feels great frustration about the small things that went wrong.
A near miss stings more than a big failure.
vocab.explanation_ko: B 씨의 비행기는 지연되어 그가 도착하기 불과 5분 전에 떠났으므로 ‘훨씬 전에(long before)’가 아니라 ‘직전에(just before)’가 알맞다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ① ‘교통 체증’ 때문에 늦었다. ③ B 씨가 더 ‘속상하다’. ④ 작은 일들에 ‘좌절감’을 느낀다. ⑤ 아깝게 놓치면 더 ‘쓰라리다’.

passage: Two men missed their flights.
Mr. A’s flight left on time, but Mr. B’s flight left just five minutes before he arrived.
Almost everyone thinks Mr. B will be more upset.
That is because it is easy for him to imagine that ______________________.
If they had taken another street, he might have made it.
The closer we are to success, the more painful a miss feels.
choices: the driver was a kind person
a small change could have made a difference
Mr. A was more upset than he was
the airport was too far from town
blank.explanation_ko: 뒤 문장(다른 길로 갔더라면 탔을지도 모른다)처럼 ‘작은 변화가 결과를 바꿀 수 있었다’고 쉽게 상상하기 때문이다.
blank.distractor_ko: ① 비행기는 실제로 지연되었다. ② 운전기사의 성격 이야기는 없다. ④ B 씨가 더 속상하다. ⑤ 공항까지의 거리가 아니라 작은 차이가 문제이다.

irrelevant.intro: Mr. A and Mr. B both missed their flights.
sentences: Mr. A’s flight left on time, thirty minutes before they arrived.
Mr. B’s flight was delayed and left only five minutes before they arrived.
Most people believe Mr. B would be more upset than Mr. A.
Limousines are much bigger and more comfortable than regular cars.
He can easily imagine how a few small changes could have saved his flight.
irrelevant.explanation_ko: ④는 리무진이 일반 차보다 크고 편하다는 내용으로, 누가 더 속상한지와 그 이유를 다루는 흐름과 무관하다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ① A 씨의 상황, ② B 씨의 상황, ③ 사람들의 판단, ⑤ B 씨가 더 속상한 이유 — 모두 흐름에 맞다.

order.given: Mr. A and Mr. B traveled in the same limousine, got caught in a traffic jam, and arrived at the airport thirty minutes late.

blocks.A: Who is more upset? Most people believe it is Mr. B. He can almost feel how close he was, thinking, “If only we had taken Main Street.”
blocks.B: When you miss a goal by a wide margin, it is hard to imagine a different result. But when you miss by just a little, it stings.
blocks.C: Mr. A is told that his flight left on time. Mr. B is told that his flight was delayed and left just five minutes ago.

order.explanation_ko: 함께 늦게 도착(주어진 글) → 두 사람이 들은 소식(C) → 누가 더 속상한가와 B 씨의 아쉬움(A) → 일반화(B) 순이다.
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 Who is more upset? 은 (C)의 두 소식을 비교하는 질문이고, (B)는 앞의 사례를 일반화하므로 맨 끝이다.

insert.insert_sentence: Mr. A is told that his flight left on time, but Mr. B is told that his flight left just five minutes ago.

passage_marked.text: Mr. A and Mr. B arrived at the airport thirty minutes after their flights were scheduled to leave.
Almost everyone answers that Mr. B is.
He can easily imagine taking a different street or stopping for a shorter time.
So many small changes could have made the outcome different.

insert.explanation_ko: 누가 더 속상한지 묻기 전에 두 사람이 들은 서로 다른 소식이 먼저 나와야 하므로 ①에 들어간다.
insert.distractor_ko: ② 이후에는 이미 질문이 나와 비교할 정보가 빠진 채가 된다. ③④⑤ 는 B 씨가 더 속상한 이유를 설명하는 흐름이다.

passage: Two men missed their flights after a traffic jam.
One flight had left on time, but the other had left just five minutes earlier.
In a survey, 96 percent of people said the second man would be more upset.
This is because he can easily imagine how things could have been different.
A different street or a shorter stop might have changed everything.
When we fail by a wide margin, such thoughts do not come easily.
But a near miss stings, because success was so close.
The closer we are to success, the more we think about what might have been.
summary.summary_template: People feel more __(A)__ when they miss a goal by a little, because they can easily imagine how small changes could have led to __(B)__.
summary.explanation_ko: 아깝게 놓치면 더 속상하고(upset), 작은 변화가 성공(success)으로 이어졌을 거라고 쉽게 상상하기 때문이다.
summary.distractor_ko: ① 편안해지는 것이 아니다. ③ 작은 변화가 이끌었을 것은 실패가 아니라 성공이다. ④ 자랑스러움이 아니다. ⑤ 지루함·위험이 아니다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.explanation_ko: 가주어 it 과 진주어 to understand why — ‘그 이유를 이해하기는 쉽다’.
writing.answer: And it’s easy to understand why.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 우리말을 영작하시오.
conditions: the + 비교급, the + 비교급 구문을 사용할 것
writing.explanation_ko: we are close to success → The closer we are to success, our minds replay … much → the more our minds replay ….
writing.answer: The closer we are to success, the more our minds replay the “what ifs.”
writing.ko_prompt: 우리가 성공에 가까울수록, 우리의 마음은 “만약 ~했더라면”을 더 많이 되풀이한다.

writing.question: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
writing.context: “If ___________ the driver hadn’t stopped so long at that particular station.”
writing.explanation_ko: If only + 과거완료 ‘~했더라면 (좋았을 텐데)’ — 과거 사실과 반대되는 아쉬움. 본문 9번 문장이다.

writing.question: 다음 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.explanation_ko: by a wide margin ‘큰 차이로’, 가주어 it ~ 진주어 to imagine, would have changed ‘바꾸었을 것이다’.
writing.en_prompt: When you miss your goal by a wide margin, it’s hard to imagine that a few differences would have changed the result.
writing.answer: 큰 차이로 목표를 놓치면, 몇 가지 차이가 결과를 바꾸었을 것이라고 상상하기는 어렵다.

writing.question: 본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Mr. B would be more __(A)__ than Mr. A, because the closer we are to __(B)__, the more we think about the “what ifs.”
writing.explanation_ko: 본문 6번 문장의 more upset than Mr. A, 13번 문장의 The closer we are to success 에서 찾는다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 이 글의 주제문을 영어로 쓰시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
conditions: success 와 closer 를 반드시 포함할 것
writing.answer: The closer we are to success, the more painful it is when we miss our goal.
writing.explanation_ko: the 비교급, the 비교급 구문으로 ‘성공에 가까울수록 놓쳤을 때 더 아프다’를 쓴다.
